terms.comment: Classically a small basin or tub.

evidence: Plaut. Curc. 2.3.33: dare aquālem cum aquā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a vessel for washing, a basin, wash-basin, ewer”, from aqua; a portable bowl or jug, not a fixed sink.

phrases.latin: Theodōrus, priusquam exīret, ad lābellum minimum manūs lāvit.
phrases.english: Before he came out, Theo washed his hands at the tiny basin.

labellum.against: Lewis & Short labellum, with a short a
labellum.html: De Vaan, s.v. lavō: lābrum < *lavābrum, whence the long ā of the diminutive.

sources: de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin (2008), s.v. lavō: lābrum < *lavābrum, whence the long ā of the diminutive.
